brief:
WHAT HAPPENED
- Voters in Israel headed to the polls in a pivotal national election focused on security and democracy.
- A temporary truce began in a war-torn Ukrainian city to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.
- Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic released a 355-page IPO prospectus warning of catastrophic risks to humankind ahead of its public market listing.
- Apple announced it will replace iPhone Duo foldable devices after online reports showed screen defects.
- UK Chancellor John Healey prepared to deliver the UK government Budget on 28 October, unveiling initial tariff cuts on staple items.

WHY IT MATTERS
- Anthropic is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO)—meaning it will sell company shares to the public on a stock exchange for the first time as a standalone AI business.
- Potential political stalemates in Israel may lead to prolonged coalition negotiations, raising regional policy uncertainty.
- Tech hardware issues can harm brand trust and trigger operational costs when consumer electronics companies must replace faulty flagship products.
- Government budgets and tariff reductions alter household import costs and set national fiscal priorities.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY
- Election results and seat counts in Israel to see whether any political bloc secures a governing majority.
- Aid delivery operations and civilian evacuation efforts under the announced Ukraine city ceasefire.
- Further market reactions to Anthropic's IPO prospectus disclosures and regulatory filings.
- Lead-up announcements and policy debates ahead of the official UK Budget delivery on 28 October.

IN SIMPLE TERMS
Voters in Israel are choosing a new government, while a local truce in Ukraine opened corridors for humanitarian aid. In technology and business, Apple is replacing damaged foldable phone screens, and AI firm Anthropic issued safety warnings in paperwork filed before selling shares to the public. Meanwhile, the UK government is rolling out initial tariff changes right before presenting its full budget.
